speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, were you wearing a seatbelt at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right hip fracture (likely femoral neck or intertrochanteric).

The mechanism of injury (restrained driver in rear-end collision) combined with immediate right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning is highly suspicious for a hip fracture. Can you confirm if your right leg appears shorter or rotated outward compared to the left?
